name: Sysco Corporation
moat_justification: Scale cost advantage as the largest US foodservice distributor (~17% share vs US Foods ~10%): purchasing terms, route/warehouse density, Sysco Brand private label, 50+ years of dividend growth and historically double-digit ROIC (Morningstar: narrow moat) — against low customer switching costs and multi-sourcing, locally fragmented competition from ~15,000 distributors plus scaled USFD/PFG, decade-flat ~18-19% gross margins (limited pricing power), labor/fuel intensity, and structural share loss of price-sensitive independents to cash-and-carry (the gap the $29.1B Jetro deal is buying into).
one_liner: Durable scale distributor, moat 6/10, with clean owner's earnings ($3.79/share, both definitions agree) — but at $79.03 (4.79% OE yield) it yields an 8.14% weighted IRR with IV@15% of $34.64, and even the Jetro-success super-bull case (12.22%) stays below the hurdle; it clears 15% only at ~$35, with ~$11.7B of net debt rising pro forma for the $29.1B Jetro deal as the key risk to watch.
moat_for: Largest US foodservice distributor (~17% share) — purchasing scale and supplier terms
Route/warehouse density lowers per-case delivery cost vs regionals
Sysco Brand private label and broadline one-stop breadth
Through-cycle compounding, 50+ years of dividend growth, historically double-digit ROIC
moat_against: Low customer switching costs; customers multi-source locally
Scaled rivals US Foods and Performance Food Group plus ~15,000 regional distributors
Gross margin stuck ~18-19% for a decade — limited pricing power
Cash-and-carry formats taking price-sensitive independents — the gap the Jetro deal buys into
